newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Thursday were seen steady to mostly $0.50 higher, instances $1.00 per cwt higher, amid outlooks for continued tight hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Hog marketings were getting smaller as more producers, particularly in the eastern Corn Belt, returned to fieldwork after being delayed by a winter-like storm late last week.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday were 107,000 head, below that day's estimate of 110,000, USDA reported. Interior receipts for Wednesday were estimated at 105,000 head, USDA said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant at interior Iowa and southern Minnesota locations could range $54.00 to $55.00 and Illinois top prices at the plant could range $54.00 to $54.50, the dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs shipped to plants could span $55.50 to $56.00, they said.
Price strength could be diluted by belief that lower pork prices on Twesday would erode packer operating margins and spur packer resistance to higher hog prices, dealers said.
Fresh pork loins at midday were quoted $2.00-$4.00 per cwt lower, USDA statistics showed.

Hams weighing 20-26 lbs were quoted $1.00-$3.00 lower, pork bellies were mostly $2.00 lower and trimmings $1.00-$4.00 lower, the statistics showed. There were 34.75 loads of pork cuts and 18.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
